summary: Describes an EPP extension for notifying clients about operations on client-sponsored objects that the client did not initiate through EPP. Examples include batch processes, customer support actions, UDRP or URS actions, and court-directed changes. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: If someone else changes your domain record, you want to be told. This is a notice system that says what changed and why.

questions: epp poll messages for domain changes
what is the epp change poll extension
what are the before and after states in epp poll
subtitle: How an EPP server tells a registrar what changed on its objects, by whom and why, when the registrar did not make the change.

tldr.problem: A client that sponsors objects such as domain names can have them changed by batch jobs, support staff, dispute actions or court orders, and the client is not involved in or aware of those changes.
tldr.mechanism: The server queues EPP poll messages that carry the object's state before and/or after the change, plus a changeData element saying what operation happened, when, who did it and optionally why.
tldr.outcome: Clients can keep their own systems in sync with the server. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 8590 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2019, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends RFC 5730 and is used alongside object mappings such as RFC 5731.

sections.title: Why Clients Need Change Notices
sections.content:
RFC 8590 is an extension to version 1.0 of the Extensible Provisioning Protocol (EPP, RFC 5730). It is used together with an object mapping such as the domain name mapping in RFC 5731. Its job is to notify a client about operations on objects the client sponsors when the client was not directly involved.

The abstract lists the kinds of operations in mind: regular batch processes, customer support actions, Uniform Domain-Name Dispute-Resolution Policy (UDRP) or Uniform Rapid Suspension (URS) actions, court-directed actions, and bulk updates based on customer requests. Which operations and which clients get a notice is up to server policy.

Notices travel as messages in the EPP poll queue. The extension only extends the EPP <poll> response; it does not extend the <poll> command.
sections.eli5: When someone other than you changes something you look after, the server leaves you a message so your own records can stay correct.

sections.title: The changeData Element
sections.content:
The extra information lives in a <changePoll:changeData> element in the extension part of the poll response. The object itself is shown in the normal resData block, so the client sees the object's state together with the operation detail: what, who, when and why.

Its children are:

  • <changePoll:operation>: the transform operation that was executed.
  • <changePoll:date>: when it was executed.
  • <changePoll:svTRID>: the server transaction identifier of the operation.
  • <changePoll:who>: who executed it.
  • <changePoll:caseId> (optional): a case identifier whose required type is udrp, urs or custom; a custom case is named with the optional name attribute.
  • <changePoll:reason> (optional): server-specific text explaining why, in the language negotiated with the client.

The who value is free-form and meant strictly for audit purposes, not to drive client-side logic. A server may base it on a user identifier, a name or a role such as CSR or Batch.
sections.eli5: Each note answers four questions: what happened, when, who did it, and sometimes why.

sections.title: Operations and Before/After State
sections.content:
The operation element holds one of an enumerated list: create, delete, renew, transfer, update, restore, autoRenew, autoDelete, autoPurge or custom. An optional op attribute refines it. A delete or autoDelete that purges the object immediately MUST set op to purge. A transfer MUST set it to request, approve, cancel or reject, and a restore MUST set it to request or report. A custom operation MUST put its name in op.

The state attribute of changeData is before or after, defaulting to after. A server MAY send both, using one poll message for each, and the before message MUST be queued first.

If an operation has no after state, such as a purge, the server MUST use the before message. If it has no before state, such as create, the server MUST use the after message.
sections.eli5: The note can show your thing as it was before the change, as it is after, or both. If the thing was thrown away there is no after, and if it was just made there is no before.

sections.title: Worked Examples in the RFC
sections.content:
Section 3.1.2 gives several example poll responses, all with result code 1301 (command completed successfully; ack to dequeue). They include a URS lock on domain.example shown once with the before state and once with the after state, a custom sync operation, an immediate purge after a delete with the reason Court order, an autoPurge of a domain with pendingDelete status, and an update to the host ns1.domain.example.

In the URS example the before message shows the domain with status ok, while the after message shows the statuses serverUpdateProhibited, serverDeleteProhibited and serverTransferProhibited. Both carry the case identifier urs123 and the reason URS Lock.
sections.eli5: The examples show real-looking notes: a domain locked by a dispute, a domain thrown away by court order, and a host that was changed.

sections.title: Dates, Commands and the Schema
sections.content:
Dates and times MUST be in UTC using the Gregorian calendar, in the extended date-time form with uppercase T and Z from XML Schema, because XML Schema does not support truncated forms or lowercase letters.

The extension adds nothing to the EPP <check>, <info> or <transfer> commands or to <create>, <delete>, <renew> and <update>. It only adds elements to the poll response.

The formal XML schema is in Section 4. It makes who a string of 1 to 255 characters and gives state a default of after. The namespace is urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:changePoll-1.0; implementations MUST NOT depend on the prefix changePoll and should use a namespace-aware XML parser.
sections.eli5: Times are written one strict way so every computer reads them the same. The rules for the note's shape are written down in a formal template.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered the XML namespace and the XML schema, both with the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:changePoll-1.0 and the IESG as registrant contact, following RFC 3688. The extension is also registered in the EPP extension registry from RFC 7451 with status Active and TLDs set to Any.
sections.eli5: The name of this extension was written in the official list so nobody else uses it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The extension provides no security services beyond those of EPP (RFC 5730) and the protocol layers EPP runs over. The security considerations of those specifications apply here as well.
sections.eli5: This note system adds no new locks. It relies on the locks EPP already has.

viz.caption: OPERATION VALUES AND THEIR OP ATTRIBUTE

items.label: Create
items.desc: Object created; only an after state exists.

items.label: Delete
items.desc: op is purge if the object is purged immediately.

items.label: Renew
items.desc: Renew operation as defined in RFC 5730.

items.label: Transfer
items.desc: op is request, approve, cancel or reject.

items.label: Update
items.desc: Update operation as defined in RFC 5730.

items.label: Auto delete
items.desc: Executed by the server; op is purge if purged immediately.

items.label: Auto purge
items.desc: Server removes an object that had pendingDelete status.

items.label: Custom
items.desc: op carries the custom name; supported ones depend on server policy.
